audit.summary: The reversed column-vectorized system invalidates Theorem2 and Algorithm2 in an exact canonical repeated-S3 case, a Major failure of the written decomposition procedure. The corrected ordering restores the intended construction/costs and is present in retained code, so no implementation failure is asserted. Application-complexity and future validation issues remain Minor.

Counterevidence: The specific hook/almost-hook examples do have polynomial dimensions in n, and Figures 2-3 are numerical timing evidence. The paper elsewhere distinguishes the practical O(n d^3) model and the general proved bounds. The objection does not show that n^7/n^13 algorithms are impossible, only that their worst-case status is not supplied by the cited displayed bound. It also does not affect polynomial complexity in the matrix input dimension d.

Limits: This is coefficient-basis orthogonality. It is not a claim of functional L2-orthogonality of monomials for every weight. The joint growth in n and p need not be polynomial in n+p, while the main bound is in the actual representation dimension. The opening phrase 'degree n' on p.1088 is locally inconsistent with the subsequent consistently used p, but no separate scientific finding is proposed.

Limits: No raw benchmark data, hardware timing replication, or author-code execution was performed. Graph inspection is not a proof of an asymptotic bound or a certified stability guarantee. Figure 3's unqualified 'predicted/at worst' rates are treated separately in L06.

proposition.claim:
The input consists of symmetric orthogonal matrices \(A_i=\rho(\tau_i)\), where \(\tau_i=(i,i+1)\) and \(\rho:S_n\to O(d)\) is a representation. The task is to identify partitions \(\lambda\), compute multiplicities \(a_\lambda\), and find an orthogonal change of basis to repeated copies of the canonical Young orthogonal representations.

The article explicitly assumes real arithmetic on p. 1070. Its proved bounds are \(O(n^2d^3)\) for identifying constituents and multiplicities and a further \(O(nd^4)\) for decoupling repeated copies. The complete stated procedure therefore has bound \[O(n^2d^3+nd^4).\] The practical \(O(nd^3)\) behavior and floating-point accuracy are separately discussed as observations or possible improvements. These claims are not interpreted as bit-complexity bounds or as an already certified floating-point implementation. Nor does polynomial dependence on the supplied matrix dimension establish polynomial complexity in a compact partition encoding of the general Kronecker-coefficient problem.

Printed Kronecker factor order is inconsistent with declared column concatenation and fails its prescribed canonical decomposition.
